supersedes: revision 1, which flagged shared hulls as problems. Sleven's ruling of 2026-08-14 makes most of them non-issues by design. See DECISION_shared-hulls-are-fine-unless-the-shape-differs-2026-08-14.md.
the_rule: The 3D viewer renders bare geometry - wireframe/hologram, no textures, no interiors. A livery difference and an interior difference are both invisible in it BY CONSTRUCTION. Therefore a shared hull is CORRECT unless the two ships differ in EXTERNAL SHAPE. Everything that distinguishes the ships otherwise - components, DPS, crew, cargo - lives on the ship page and comes from CIG's data.
what_this_means_for_flags: Sharing a model is not a defect and is not shown to the reader. Only an external-shape disagreement is.
how_shape_is_tested: CIG's published length, width, height and mass from ship_specs.json. This is a PROXY and a weak one: two ships can share an envelope and still differ in shape. It is what is available. Anyone who compares two of these in game beats it.

verdicts.shape_defect: the geometry contradicts an external-shape claim. Show the reader.
verdicts.shape_inconsistent: the geometry disagrees with CIG's own published figures. Show the reader.
verdicts.shared_hull_ok: shares a model with another ship. Under the rule above this is correct and is NOT shown to the reader. Recorded so it is not re-flagged as a bug by the next pass.

flagged.why: A docked C8X snub is an EXTERNAL shape difference - the one kind the viewer can actually show. These files are byte-identical to Carrack.glb, so they do not contain it. This survives the rule because the difference is geometric, not livery and not interior.
flagged.open_question: whether a correct Carrack-with-snub model exists anywhere. Ours is not one; that a better one is obtainable was never established.

flagged.why: Not a shared-hull case - the reverse. Four Aurora Mk I variants share one 267,000-vertex model; the LX has its own 28,153-vertex model. Its measured height is 3.733 against 4.355 for the shared model, while CIG publishes 4.5 m height for EVERY Aurora Mk I variant including the LX. The file that does not share disagrees with CIG; the four that do share match.

Sleven, 2026-08-14: the Privateer and the Kraken look near-identical in CIG's own concept art; the differences are internal. No published dimensions exist for either, but under the rule the shared hull is fine and the two ship pages carry the real differences.
